title: Testing the booking core
idea: A test case is code that sets up known state, calls one behaviour, and checks the result, so a wrong rule fails loudly before users find it.
points: Each test builds fresh state (arrange), calls once (act), then checks one result (assert).
Bugs hide at boundaries: touching slots, zero length, other rooms, wrong owner.
Assert the stable `code()` of an exception, not its message text, which may change.
Replace email and audit with a recording fake to check which events fired.

code.title: Rule tests at the boundaries
code.caption: A tiny hand-written runner standing in for JUnit 5. Each case states its expected error code.

walk.text: Each test reads as a sentence: name, expected outcome, one action. The table becomes code.
Arrange: every test gets a new service with ana's 09:00 booking. Tests cannot leak state.
Act: run the action once. Map success to `OK` and failures to their stable `code()`.
Assert: compare codes, and print what actually happened so a failure explains itself.
The rule under test. `start >= end` covers both reversed and zero-length slots.
Strict less-than on both sides makes slots half-open, so back-to-back bookings pass.

code.title: A fake listener for events
code.caption: Teams use Mockito here; a hand-written fake does the same job and shows the idea clearly.

walk.text: The fake is injected exactly like `NotificationService` would be. The service cannot tell the difference.
The most valuable test: a rejected booking must not notify anyone.
Checking the full list also checks order: booked first, cancelled second.
The fake only records strings. No network, no clock, so the test is deterministic.
Listeners fire only after the save. Notify before the clash check and the second test fails.

pitfalls: Sharing one service across tests makes results depend on run order; build fresh state each time.
Testing only the happy path misses back-to-back and zero-length slots, where real bugs live.
Asserting on exception messages breaks tests on rewording; assert the `code()` instead.

quiz.q: Ana holds R1 from 9.0 to 10.0. What does this print?
options: PASS starts at 10 (OK), PASS ends at 9 (ROOM_TAKEN)
PASS starts at 10 (OK), FAIL ends at 9 (OK)
FAIL starts at 10 (ROOM_TAKEN), PASS ends at 9 (OK)
quiz.why: Slots are half-open, so 8.0-9.0 only touches 9.0-10.0 and is booked. The second test encodes a wrong expectation: tests can be wrong too.

takeaway: Fresh state, one action, one stable assertion, and every boundary covered.
